newsitem.title: USA: Consumers says 780 MW nuke may restart Sun.
newsitem.headline: Consumers says 780 MW nuke may restart Sun.

text.p: Consumers Power Co's 780 megawatt Palisades nuclear power plant may resume electrical production Feb 9 after shutting down to repair an electrical problem, a company spokesman said Monday.
"Feb 9 is our target date (for synchronizing to the electricity grid)," spokesman Mark Savage said.
The plant, located in South Haven, Mich., was shut Jan 23 to repair an electrical connection at a main generator.
The plant is being kept in a hot shutdown mode, eliminating the need for several days of restart testing before synchronizing to the power grid, the spokesman said.
The unit is expected to take several days to reach full power once it is hooked to the grid, Savage said.
The Palisades plant makes up about 18 percent of Consumers' power generation capacity.
Consumers Power is a subsidiary of CMS Energy Corp.
